text:
anna (support): FYI escalation from Acme. After yesterday's billing cutover they report dashboard shows missing series + tooltips pointing at the wrong lines on mobile. They also saw a couple of 502s when hitting /v1/metrics. Screenshot: https://s3.redwood-inference/customer-acme/esc-1234/screen1.png :exclamation:

mike (frontend): Thanks. Is this only mobile or also on web? can you paste repro steps + account id?

anna (support): Account: acme-corp-42. Repro we got from customer (short): 1) Log into console 2) Open Project > Analytics > Hourly Ingest 3) Switch to last 24h 4) On iPhone Safari the legend order doesn't match the colored lines, tapping legend highlights wrong series. On web the colors are correct but last 2 hours show "No data" even though ingestion logs exist. They mentioned the issue started right after a billing webhook at 2026-03-15T09:03Z.

sophie (metrics): Pasted a couple of relevant logs from infra:
```
2026-03-15T09:03:04Z metrics-ingest svc ERROR 403 "billing: account suspended" user=acme-corp-42
2026-03-15T09:03:12Z metrics-proxy svc WARN 502 upstream timeout route=/v1/metrics query="range=24h"
2026-03-15T09:05:00Z metrics-ingest svc INFO 200 batch=2500 src=kinesis
```
Looks like a short auth failure window; dropped points are ~2k.

sam (mobile): I can repro on iPhone 12 / Safari 16.4. Weird CSS + order issue: when legend becomes vertically stacked the flex order uses the series array index, but the chart rendering library reorders series by timestamp of last point. On mobile that mismatch causes the legend index -> series id mapping to be incorrect. Quick repro CSS hack: `ul.legend { flex-wrap: nowrap; }` avoids the wrap and keeps order consistent.

mike (frontend): That matches a bug I saw in the recent color-key refactor. We changed the legend mapping to rely on `document.querySelectorAll('.series')` order which is not stable when the chart reorders series after data arrives. Proposed quick server-side workaround: serve stable `seriesKey` in payload and use that for legend mapping.

anna (support): Customer also reported occasional "Failed to fetch metrics (502)" banner before page shows "No data" — they want root cause and ETA. This was escalated to P1 due to product impact.

sophie (metrics): Metric-level root cause: short billing auth rejection caused the ingestion pipeline to drop a handful of batches. When data resumed, the chart library merged new series and shifted ordering. The front-end code lost the stable id -> color mapping for reordered series. I think two fixes: (1) hotfix front-end to use explicit `seriesKey` mapping, (2) reconcile missing points by requerying range with devtools API (backfill) — but backfill is more invasive.

ops-bot: deploy requested: redwood/frontend#hotfix/legend-stable-1837 -> staging

mike (frontend): I'm pushing a small patch to use `seriesKey` mapping and guard legend clicks by series id rather than index. PR: https://git.redwood/FE/pulls/5123. Will patch CSS for mobile wrap as fallback.

anna (support): Can someone confirm QA steps? Customer will need a workaround in the meantime.

mike (frontend): QA steps:
1) With a project that has >=3 series, open Analytics > Hourly > Last 24h on iPhone Safari
2) Force a short ingest gap (we can simulate by toggling billing flag in local dev) or use the test fixture at `/test/ingest/gap`
3) Verify legend order remains matched to the colored lines after data resumes; tap legend items to highlight corresponding series.

sophie (metrics): I can trigger a requery/backfill for acme-corp-42 to restore the missing points if product approves. That will remove the "No data" holes.

anna (support): Assigned to oncall and frontend. Jira: RDW-ESC-2217. Marked P1, customer notified that we're working on a hotfix for the legend/tooltips and will follow up on data backfill. I'll send a short status update to acme.

mike (frontend): Hotfix merged to staging, will monitor for 30m then deploy to prod. If anyone sees repeated 502s from metrics-proxy after deploy, ping `@ops`.

anna (support): Thanks all. I'll post the customer-facing update here when sent. :white_check_mark:
